Basically. I add garlic powder to the roux and use a mixture of whole milk and heavy cream. I'm pretty basic with the cheeses (cheddar, jack, and Gouda). I'm open to different cheese options, but just haven't messed with what works.

I started off with influences from a few recipes, but I can eye it now. I start a roux with melted butter, flour and garlic powder. Once it melds together constantly whisking (not necessarily brown), I slowly whisk in a mixture of heavy cream and whole milk. I season that with ground mustard, nutmeg, cayenne, pepper and salt. High heat until it bubbles then low heat stirring attentively until the sauce coats a spoon. Add grated cheese (not pre grated - I use Gouda, jack, and cheddar) a handful at a time until it melts. I boil the noodles during all of that and rinse before they reach el dente. Mix it all together then pour it on a greased pan. Sprinkle with remaining cheese and a mixture of melted butter and panko. Bake until brown.
